headline: Nigeria: a 23% policy rate versus 3% in the UEMOA, two monetary worlds
summary: The Central Bank of Nigeria kept its benchmark rate at 23%, extending a restrictive stance aimed at consolidating disinflation and defending naira stability. The article contrasts this with the BCEAO's 3% rate in the UEMOA zone.
why: Nigeria's central bank sets monetary policy for Africa's largest economy, and its rate decisions shape naira exchange rates, bond yields and local borrowing costs.
original_headline: Nigeria : un taux directeur de 23 %, contre 3 % dans l’UEMOA, deux mondes monétaires
